question.problem:
For the functions $h(x)$ and $z(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
h(5)=5,\,{h}^{′}(5)=-3,\,z(5)=-6,\,{z}^{′}(5)=8
$$

If $w(x)=(h(x)+z(x))(3h(x)-10)$, compute ${w}^{′}(5).$
question.worked_solution:
The product rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(uv)=u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=h(x)+z(x)$ and $v=3h(x)-10.$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={h}^{′}(x)+{z}^{′}(x)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=3{h}^{′}(x).
$$

Substituting this into the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}^{′}(x) & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =({h}^{′}(x)+{z}^{′}(x))(3h(x)-10)+(h(x)+z(x))(3{h}^{′}(x)) \\  & =({h}^{′}(x)+{z}^{′}(x))(3h(x)-10)+3{h}^{′}(x)(h(x)+z(x)).\end{aligned}
$$

At $x=5$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}^{′}(5) & =({h}^{′}(5)+{z}^{′}(5))(3h(5)-10)+3{h}^{′}(5)(h(5)+z(5)) \\  & =(-3+8)\cdot (3\cdot 5-10)+3\cdot (-3)\cdot (5+(-6)) \\  & =5\cdot 5+3\cdot (-3)\cdot (-1) \\  & =34.\end{aligned}
$$
